name: tsa_getOrderByToken
description: Returns the order behind a QR token, joined to worker, restaurant and meal, for restaurant staff to verify before redeeming. Zero rows when the token is unknown. Called by GET. Called by the TSA Eats Next.js app (tsa-eats/lib/api.ts) through api/Endpoints/TsaApi.cs, which maps queryType 'getOrderByToken' to [TSA].[tsa_getOrderByToken]. There is no Harrier Central auth: POST requires the shared X-Api-Key (TsaApiKey); GET requires nothing, and the shim does not restrict which procedure a GET may name. The shim turns any one-row rowset with Success = 0 into HTTP 400 {success:false, errorMessage}, and an empty first rowset into HTTP 404.

columns.name: redeemedAt
columns.description: Redemption time, CONVERT style 127 of a DATETIME2 UTC value — ISO text with no 'Z' or offset; NULL if not redeemed.

codeSmells.detail: @token (line 2) have no SQL default. A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the body runs: no log row, and the TsaApi shim returns a generic 500.

codeSmells.issue: SP body not wrapped in TRY/CATCH
codeSmells.detail: Read procedure with no TRY/CATCH: any runtime error (timeout, deadlock) becomes an unlogged raw 500 from the shim.

Line 24 formats TSA.Order.redeemedAt (DATETIME2, GETUTCDATE()) with style 127, which carries no 'Z'; JavaScript parses it as local time. TSA.Order uses DATETIME2 where every other TSA table uses DATETIMEOFFSET.
Called by GET with no key; anyone holding a token sees the worker's full name. Tokens are random GUIDs, so this is exposure by token, not enumeration.
